newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zambian agency invites bids for Maamba Collieries.
newsitem.headline: Zambian agency invites bids for Maamba Collieries.

text.p: The Zambian Privatisation Agency (ZPA) has offered the majority share of the country's only coal mine, Maamba Collieries Ltd (MCL), for sale under the country's privatisation programme.
In adverts in South African newspapers, ZPA invited offers for the acquisition of at least 70 percent of the mine's shareholding.
It said the closing date for bid submissions was December 13.
ZPA said a four-month due diligence period has been provided for bidders to probe and evaluate all information pertaining to MCL.
Interested bidders will have to conduct their own exploration and analysis, ZPA added.

The privatisation agency said the mine had 60.2 million tonnes of coal in proven reserves while a total of 78.2 million tonnes were estimated to be available in the MCL assigned area in southern Zambia.
Two open cast mines at Maamba, 352 km south of the Zambian capital Lusaka, had an annual production capacity of 600,000 to 800,000 tonnes of coal.
It said the company had a ready local market for coal, including major copper producer Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd (ZCCM).
The ZPA said MCL also exported coal to Malawi, Tanzania and Zaire.
Zambia last month invited pre-qualification bids for Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd's (ZCCM) assets as part of the country's privatisation drive.
Zambia produced around 380,000 tonnes of copper last year, making it the world's seventh largest producer. The government said in June it expected copper output to treble following privatisation.
